extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy (esp. empiricism/John Locke)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts Locke's central methodological and epistemological claims about the origins of ideas and how the understanding acquires knowledge, as presented in Book II of An Essay Concerning Human Understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge depends on right use of our faculties, not innate principles
rubrics_metrics.description: OUR KNOWLEDGE DEPENDS UPON THE RIGHT USE OF THOSE POWERS NATURE HATH BESTOWED UPON US, and how little upon SUCH INNATE PRINCIPLES AS ARE IN VAIN SUPPOSED TO BE IN ALL MANKIND FOR THEIR DIRECTION; which all men could not but know if they were there, or else they would be there to no purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If purported innate principles are not universally known, they are useless; instead, employ and examine one's own faculties to obtain real knowledge rather than relying on assumed innate truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Men must think and know for themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: I have not made it my business either to quit or follow any authority in the ensuing Discourse. Truth has been my only aim; and wherever that has appeared to lead, my thoughts have impartially followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give due respect to others' opinions but prioritize seeking truth through one's own impartial reasoning rather than unexamined assent to authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek truth in consideration of things themselves
rubrics_metrics.description: Perhaps we should make greater progress in the discovery of rational and contemplative knowledge, if we sought it in the fountain, IN THE CONSIDERATION OF THINGS THEMSELVES; and made use rather of our own thoughts than other men’s to find it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid attempting to 'know by other men's understandings' — use direct consideration and personal reasoning as the primary path to knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspicion of innate principles and explanation of their origin
rubrics_metrics.description: When men have found some general propositions that could not be doubted of as soon as understood, it was... a short and easy way to conclude them innate. This... eased the lazy from the pains of search, and stopped the inquiry of the doubtful concerning all that was once styled innate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of labeling propositions 'innate' merely because they seem obvious; that label can be used to discourage inquiry and consolidate authority over learners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design of the discourse: show how understanding proceeds
rubrics_metrics.description: To show HOW the understanding proceeds herein is the design of the following Discourse; which I shall proceed to when I have first premised... the reasons I had to doubt of innate principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological aim: give an account of the origins and formation of ideas and the workings of the understanding, grounded in observation and experience rather than presupposed axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea is the object of thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Every man being conscious to himself that he thinks; and that which his mind is applied about whilst thinking being the IDEAS that are there, it is past doubt that men have in their minds several ideas...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations into knowledge begin by asking how ideas (the objects of thought) come to be in the mind.

rubrics_metrics.name: All ideas come from Sensation or Reflection
rubrics_metrics.description: To this I answer, in one word, from EXPERIENCE. ... Our observation employed either, about external sensible objects, or about the internal operations of our minds perceived and reflected on by ourselves, is that which supplies our understandings with all the MATERIALS of thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject the notion of innate ideas; classify all ideas as derived from either external sensory experience or internal reflection upon mental operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensation as a source of ideas (definition and examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Senses, conversant about particular sensible objects, do convey into the mind several distinct perceptions of things... by which we come by those IDEAS we have of yellow, white, heat, cold, soft, hard, bitter, sweet, and all those which we call sensible qualities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensation = external objects affecting the senses and thereby producing perceptions; sensory qualities are imprinted on the mind via sensation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reflection as a source of ideas (internal sense)
rubrics_metrics.description: The other fountain... is,—the perception of the operations of our own mind within us, as it is employed about the ideas it has got... such are perception, thinking, doubting, believing, reasoning, knowing, willing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflection (internal sense) yields ideas of mental operations; these are distinct from sensible qualities and arise when the mind attends to its own operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: All our ideas are of one or the other source
rubrics_metrics.description: The understanding seems to me not to have the least glimmering of any ideas which it doth not receive from one of these two. EXTERNAL OBJECTS furnish the mind with the ideas of sensible qualities... and THE MIND furnishes the understanding with ideas of its own operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing any idea, trace its origin to either sensation or reflection; Locke treats these as jointly exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas are acquired by degrees (observable in children)
rubrics_metrics.description: He that attentively considers the state of a child, at his first coming into the world, will have little reason to think him stored with plenty of ideas... It is BY DEGREES he comes to be furnished with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical evidence: children's development supports the claim that ideas accumulate over time through interaction with the environment and reflections thereon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differential furnishing of minds according to objects and attention
rubrics_metrics.description: Men then come to be furnished with fewer or more simple ideas from without, according as the objects they converse with afford greater or less variety; and from the operations of their minds within, according as they more or less reflect on them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variation in ideas across people is explained by differences in sensory environments and the degree to which individuals attend to and reflect on their mental operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas of reflection appear later because they require attention
rubrics_metrics.description: And hence we see the reason why it is pretty late before most children get ideas of the operations of their own minds; ... till the understanding turns inward upon itself, reflects on its own operations, and makes them the objects of its own contemplation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predicts developmental timeline: reflective ideas require inward attention and so typically emerge after sensory ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas (perception) begin with sensation — definition of sensation
rubrics_metrics.description: If it shall be demanded then, WHEN a man BEGINS to have any ideas, I think the true answer is,—WHEN HE FIRST HAS ANY SENSATION. ... SENSATION... SUCH AN IMPRESSION OR MOTION MADE IN SOME PART OF THE BODY, AS MAKES IT BE TAKEN NOTICE OF IN THE UNDERSTANDING.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sensory impression is the first source of ideas; thus the origin of ideas is temporally tied to first sensory experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: The soul does not necessarily always think; claims need proof
rubrics_metrics.description: I confess myself... that doth not perceive itself always to contemplate ideas; nor can conceive it any more necessary for the soul always to think, than for the body always to move... We know certainly, by experience, that we SOMETIMES think; and thence draw this infallible consequence—that there is something in us that has a power to think.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique of doctrines claiming continuous activity of the soul: Locke demands empirical proof rather than assumption or definitional smuggling.

rubrics_metrics.name: If the soul thinks without consciousness, absurd consequences follow (identity problem)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the soul doth think in a sleeping man without being conscious of it, I ask whether, during such thinking, it has any pleasure or pain, or be capable of happiness or misery? ... If we take wholly away all consciousness of our actions and sensations... it will be hard to know wherein to place personal identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that unconscious thinking undermines the unity of personal identity and leads to paradoxical conclusions (e.g., a sleeping and waking man as two persons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dreams and memory do not plausibly support the claim that the soul always thinks
rubrics_metrics.description: That the soul in a sleeping man should be this moment busy a thinking, and the next moment in a waking man not remember nor be able to recollect one jot of all those thoughts, is very hard to be conceived... Most men, I think, pass a great part of their sleep without dreaming.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses empirical observation about dreaming and memory to challenge the hypothesis that the soul is always actively thinking in ways unremembered by the waking person.

rubrics_metrics.name: The original of all our knowledge: impressions from outward objects and the mind's own operations
rubrics_metrics.description: The impressions then that are made on our sense by outward objects that are extrinsical to the mind; and its own operations about these impressions, reflected on by itself, as proper objects to be contemplated by it, are, I conceive, the original of all knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary principle: knowledge arises from two fountains — sensation (external impressions) and reflection (internal operations) — which together provide the materials for all human ideas and intellectual development.
